test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Though the speaker used flowery expressions to convince the audience, they were intelligent enough __to find out his ulterior intentions. __

options.text: to not judge a book by its cover

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **to read between the lines**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"To read between the lines"** means to understand the hidden meaning or subtext of something. (छिपे हुए या अप्रकटित अर्थ को समझना)

 
 
• **Example:** You need to read between the lines to understand what the author is truly saying.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **to read between the lines**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To cast pearls before swine** (मूर्खों के सामने मूल्यवान वस्तु प्रस्तुत करना): Offering valuable things to those who can't appreciate them.

 
 
• **Example:** Sharing profound wisdom with uninterested students is like casting pearls before swine.
 
 
 
• **To not judge a book by its cover** (केवल बाहरी रूप देखकर किसी का मूल्यांकन न करना): Avoid judging based on appearances.
 
 
• **Example:** That old house looks shabby, but don't judge a book by its cover; inside it's beautiful.
 
 
 
• **To be under somebody’s thumb** (किसी के नियंत्रण या प्रभाव में होना): Being dominated or controlled by someone.
 
 
• **Example:** John is under his wife’s thumb and rarely makes decisions on his own.
 
 

13e:Tcab,
The correct answer is **Option 1**.
